title: Image-pull congestion -> eviction wave (postmortem draft)
content:
Summary:

On 2025-11-02 between 03:12-03:50 UTC we experienced a widespread pod eviction wave affecting three availability zones. Symptoms: large number of pods in CrashLoopBackOff / ImagePullBackOff, node eviction events (kubelet invoked eviction due to ephemeral-storage and DiskPressure), and autoscaler thrash as new nodes were launched then quickly filled with failed pulls. Impact: ~28% of API-serving replicas across two services were down for ~18 minutes; P99 latency spiked, and some background batch jobs were permanently retried. Total customer-facing errors were limited but internal dashboards showed degraded capacity and increased latency for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Immediate visible trigger:
- ImagePullBackOff spikes coincided with a flurry of deploys from a canary job and a CICD surge at 03:10 UTC.
- Registry (third-party) returned 429 / 503 intermittently for concurrent pulls.
- Nodes started reporting image pull timeouts; kubelet image GC kicked in; ephemeral-storage eviction thresholds tripped on 6 nodes.

Timeline (abridged):
- 03:05 UTC: Canary deploy job triggered 120 parallel pod creations across clusters (internal job misconfigured to parallelize).
- 03:09 UTC: Monitoring alerts: registry error rate up (external), Kubernetes events show burst of ImagePullBackOffs.
- 03:12 UTC: On-call paged. First mitigation: pause CICD job (03:15).
- 03:16 UTC: Operators attempted manual pre-pull on new nodes; many pulls still returned 429.
- 03:20 UTC: Kubelet started aggressive image GC on high-churn nodes; some nodes freed space but reclaimed layers were needed by restarted pods which attempted pulls again.
- 03:25 UTC: Cluster-autoscaler launched additional nodes to satisfy pending pods; new nodes immediately saturated with image pulls and experienced the same failures.
- 03:33 UTC: Temporary mitigation — scale back replica counts for non-critical deployments (03:35); roll out an emergency DaemonSet to pre-pull a small whitelist set of images to reduce registry pressure (03:40).
- 03:50 UTC: Registry rate recovered, ImagePullBackOffs cleared and evicted pods were rescheduled. Full traffic normalized by 04:10 UTC.

Root cause analysis (contributing factors):
1) CICD misconfiguration: a scheduled canary job created ~120 pod creations concurrently across the cluster. The job had an aggressive concurrency setting that should have been bounded.
2) No registry pull-through cache or regional mirror in the affected regions. All nodes pulled directly from the upstream registry (hosted third-party) which had rate limits and started returning 429/503 under burst load.
3) Kubelet eviction thresholds + image GC interaction: our eviction thresholds for ephemeral-storage are conservative, and kubelet image GC policy was configured to be reactive. When image pulls stalled, kubelet attempted to reclaim space which caused churn (delete/pull) and created additional pull pressure.
4) Autoscaler feedback loop: autoscaler responded to pending pods by adding nodes but these nodes immediately tried to pull the same images, magnifying the registry pressure.
5) Lack of circuit-breaker on image pull failures: controllers kept retrying without backoff and created many concurrent retries. Some retry behavior came from the CICD job and from controllers that requeued pod creation when image pull failed.

Why disk pressure/evictions occurred:
- Failed pulls partially pulled blobs and wrote temporary layers; combined with existing freed space heuristics, kubelet judged nodes under ephemeral-storage pressure.
- Because image GC deleted images that other pods needed, those pods re-triggered pulls, leading to a cycle.

Immediate mitigation performed during incident (ordered):
- Paused the CICD canary job (03:15).
- Temporarily scaled down non-critical stateless services to reduce concurrent pulls (03:35).
- Deployed emergency pre-pull DaemonSet targeting a critical image whitelist to nodes in affected AZs to stabilize commonly used images (03:40).
- Increased kubelet image pull timeout to reduce rapid retries (hotfix on 03:28), and temporarily disabled aggressive image GC on the most affected nodes to avoid churn (03:30).
- Opened support case with registry provider; they acknowledged a regional rate-limiting event.

Long-term mitigations / action items (owners and tentative ETA):
- (Infra) Implement regional pull-through registry mirror (artifactory/registry-cache) + healthcheck and fallback, ETA Q1 2026. Owner: Rahul Mehta.
- (CICD) Add rate-limits and concurrency caps on deploy jobs; default to serialized canaries with a small concurrency window, ETA 2 weeks. Owner: Lina Fernández.
- (SRE) Add image-pull circuit-breaker: controller-level backoff policy + admission webhook to throttle creates if clusterwide pull-failure rate exceeds threshold, ETA 6 weeks. Owner: Jonah Kim.
- (SRE/Platform) Pre-pull DaemonSet as an opt-in for critical services and for bootstrap on new nodes; tie into node lifecycle hooks to reduce immediate mass pulls, ETA 4 weeks. Owner: Eliot Zhang.
- (SRE) Revisit kubelet eviction thresholds and image GC policy; test on staging with simulated registry failures, ETA 3 weeks. Owner: Asha Patel.
- (Monitoring) Dashboard: add "cluster image-pull failure rate" panel, surface per-registry and per-AZ error codes, and add an alert when ImagePullBackOff > N% across cluster for M minutes. ETA 1 week. Owner: Observability team.

Runbook / on-call playbook (short):
1) If ImagePullBackOff alerts trigger across >10% of nodes: pause any concurrent CI/CD push or automated deploys immediately.
2) Check registry provider status page and open support case with correlation evidence.
   - kubectl get events --all-namespaces | grep ImagePullBackOff
   - kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep ImagePullBackOff
   - journalctl -u kubelet | grep -E "pulling image|Get .* 429|error pulling image" -n 500
3) Assess whether evictions are due to ephemeral-storage or node resource pressure: kubectl describe node <node> and check kubelet eviction events.
4) If many nodes are under DiskPressure, consider temporarily disabling image GC on a small subset of nodes and pre-pull critical images via a DaemonSet.
5) If autoscaler is adding nodes that immediately fail pulls, pause autoscaler or set a scaling limiter for the affected ASG.
6) Execute quick mitigation: scale down non-essential deployments, apply emergency pre-pull DaemonSet (whitelist), and ensure kubelet timeouts/backoffs are increased.
7) After registry recovery, allow nodes to stabilise and slowly roll up deployments. Confirm with histograms: successful pulls per minute and pod restart rates.

Monitoring & dashboards to check during incidents:
- Per-node image pull errors (new panel).
- Registry error codes by AZ (429/503 counts).
- Kubelet eviction events by reason (ephemeral-storage, diskpressure).
- Autoscaler scaling events and pending pods backlog.
- Pod restart loops and CrashLoopBackOff counts.

Logs & commands we used (examples):
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 200
- kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[*].state.waiting.reason}\n' | grep ImagePullBackOff
- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-2-45.ec2.internal | egrep -A3 "Conditions|Events"
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 1000 | grep -i "image pull" -n || true
- crictl images | wc -l; crictl ps -a | head

Post-incident notes / open tickets (short):
- JIRA INC-4921: Incident record and root-cause summary (linked).
- INFRA-337: Implement registry mirror and healthchecks.
- SRE-412: Image-pull backoff/circuit-breaker design doc.
- CICD-129: Add concurrency limits to canary jobs and deploy pipelines.

Outstanding questions / discussion points:
- How aggressive should backoff be before we throttle deploys cluster-wide?
- Should node bootstrap include a small set of pre-cached base images by default?
- Do we keep an autoscaler gating mechanism to avoid creating nodes when we detect upstream registry degraded?

Appendix: reproducibility test plan (staging)
- Simulate registry returning 429 with a pull-through proxy; schedule 200 parallel pod starts and monitor image pull error rate, node eviction counts, and autoscaler behavior.
- Evaluate various kubelet image GC thresholds to identify sweet spot where disk pressure is managed without inducing churn.
- Test pre-pull DaemonSet startup ordering to ensure nodes are not overwhelmed on join.

Notes to self / TODO during writeup:
- Collect exact container image digests and node names for final postmortem.
